learningObjectives: Explain the role of Data Objects in grouping related fields
Describe the four Data Relationship types: Embedded Data, Data reference, Case reference, and Query
Select the correct relationship type and cardinality for a given scenario

elements.description: A structure that groups related fields to model a single entity and establish common context (e.g., a Customer grouping First name, Last name, Email, Phone). Data objects are reusable across an application's Case Types.

elements.text: Data relationships in Pega are like a library catalog: each book (data object) has its own record, and the catalog links books to topics, authors, and borrowers. An Embedded data relationship is like a book with a built-in bookmark ribbon — the data only makes sense inside that specific book. A Page List is like a card catalog drawer — one card per item, all managed together.

elements.description: You can extend a data object by referencing another data object; the referenced object's fields become part of the referencing object. Any object can be referenced once or many times.

Prefer a suitable existing data object, extend it when necessary, and create a new one when none fits. Related objects can be nested. Source records locally in Pega or externally; Case participants can also enter Case-owned values without a system of record.

A container that associates related fields. Unlike a data object or field, it does NOT store data — it relates data-storing elements to the elements that need that data to resolve a Case (object↔Case, object↔object, or Case↔Case).

elements.term: Single record vs. list of records
elements.description: Two ways a data relationship references data:
items: SINGLE RECORD — one related set of fields and values.
LIST OF RECORDS — multiple related records. A list Data Page uses pxResults; an embedded Page List uses its own property name and indexed entries.

elements.caption: The four Data Relationship types differ by where data is stored (Case vs external) and whether it can hold one or many records.

elements.description: Use Embedded Data to capture Case-specific input. The values are owned by the Case rather than shared source records. Ownership does not specify a universal physical table layout; the Academy credit-card example describes a persisted keyed record associated with the Case.

Use when you need to REUSE another data object from OUTSIDE the Case — data sourced from locally-stored Data Records or an external system of record (e.g., reference the facility where a medical appointment is booked).
Use when you want to REUSE data from another CASE (e.g., a user selects from a list of Service Cases from the Service Case Type).

Use for READ-ONLY access to information that is external to the Case; the Query Field Type allows PARAMETERS to query for specific data (e.g., return a medical professional's next appointment, or all appointments in a given time frame).

examPitfalls.title: A data relationship stores no data
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Do not confuse the relationship definition with stored field values. Embedded Data is Case-owned; Data reference associates maintained records. Neither the conceptual definition nor ownership establishes a universal physical database layout.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Separate relationship definition, value ownership, and configured persistence.

examPitfalls.title: Choose Field Type by source
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question presents a scenario and asks which field type (embedded vs. related) to use. Candidates choose based on complexity. The decision is based on data source: embedded data travels WITH the Case; related (sourced) data comes from an external system or Data Page.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: In-case input → Embedded; external object reuse → Data reference; another Case → Case reference; parameterized read-only lookup → Query.

examPitfalls.title: Query vs. Data reference
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Both pull external data, but Query is READ-ONLY and PARAMETERIZED for specific results, while Data reference reuses a whole data object.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Need a parameter-driven, read-only result set → Query; need to reuse an external object's fields → Data reference.

examPitfalls.title: Embedded data is stored with the Case
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Case closure is not the same as deleting data. Embedded values are persisted for the Case; their physical layout and retention depend on configuration.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use Embedded Data for Case-specific input; inspect persistence and retention instead of assuming a single work-object row.

examPitfalls.title: Single vs. list cardinality
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question describes a field that holds multiple related items and asks which page type to use. Candidates say 'Page' (single). A single related object = Page; multiple related objects = Page List — cardinality determines the page type.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Match cardinality to page type: one related object = Page (Single Record); multiple ordered objects = Page List (List of Records); keyed unordered set = Page Group.

examPitfalls.title: Object-to-object relationships
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Single record and List of records describe cardinality, not Field Types. Choose Embedded Data, Data reference, Case reference or Query, then configure one or many related records.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Nest objects via relationships; e.g., Product (Data reference) inside Product line, then Product line (Embedded, List) in the order.

examPitfalls.title: Embedded vs. referenced data — mutability
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates assume embedded data objects can be freely shared across cases; embedded data is local to the case and has no independent lifecycle.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Choose Case-owned input versus maintained reusable records deliberately. A Data reference can use local Pega records or an external source.

examPitfalls.title: Page vs. Page List vs. Page Group
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks which clipboard structure to use when storing an ordered collection of related items. Candidates select Page Group. Page Group uses keys (unordered, key-value); Page List is an ordered indexed collection — use Page List for ordered items.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Page = single embedded or referenced object. Page List = ordered list (integer-indexed) of multiple objects of the same type. Page Group = keyed map of objects. Use Page List when order matters; use Page Group when you need named-key lookups.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA describes two properties of a data relationship: 'It links two data-storing elements together, and it does NOT store the actual values itself.' A team member confuses this with a 'Data reference' relationship type. What is the correct distinction?

options.text: A data relationship is the CATEGORY (the concept) describing how fields are associated; Embedded Data, Data reference, Case reference, and Query are the TYPES of data relationship — specific implementations of that concept
A data relationship and a Data reference are synonymous in Pega — the term 'data relationship' was renamed to 'Data reference' in Pega Infinity
A data relationship stores the actual field values; a Data reference only stores a pointer (key) to the external system where values live
A data relationship is a Dev Studio concept; Data reference is the App Studio term for the same thing — the distinction is studio, not concept

practiceQuiz.hint: Is 'data relationship' the category or one specific type?
practiceQuiz.rationale: A data relationship is the overarching concept — any association between data elements that stores no data itself. The four types (Embedded Data, Data reference, Case reference, Query) are specific implementations of that concept.

optionExplanations.A: Data relationship is the umbrella concept; Data reference is one supported type.
optionExplanations.B: The category was not simply renamed to one of its specific types.
optionExplanations.C: This reverses the conceptual distinction between association and stored field values.
optionExplanations.D: The difference is category versus type, not the Studio used to view it.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An order Case captures a delivery address (street, city, postal code) typed in by the user. The address belongs only to that order, with exactly one delivery address per order. Which Field Type and cardinality are correct?

options.text: Embedded Data, Single record — user-entered, Case-specific data with one address group per order
Data reference, List of records — select multiple shared address-book records
Case reference, Single record — reference an independently processed Address Case
Query, List of records — display existing addresses from a read-only lookup

practiceQuiz.hint: The address is entered into this Case and only one address group is required.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Embedded Data captures the Case-owned delivery address. Single record matches the one-address requirement. A shared address-book reference, another Case, or read-only query would describe a different source and usage.

optionExplanations.A: The user-entered delivery address belongs to this order, with one address group.
optionExplanations.B: A shared address-book list would have a different source and cardinality.
optionExplanations.C: The address is a data group, not an independently processed Case.
optionExplanations.D: A read-only lookup does not collect the address typed into this order.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An order Case must associate a Customer whose record is maintained in an external CRM. Each order has exactly one customer. The customer data must not be duplicated inside the order. Which Field Type and cardinality?

options.text: Data reference, Single record — reuses the externally maintained Customer object; one per order
Embedded Data, Single record — the customer details are entered freshly by the user for each order
Query, Single record — fetches the customer read-only with parameters from the CRM
Case reference, Single record — references a separate Customer Case in Pega

practiceQuiz.hint: Reusing a data object from outside the Case = Data reference; one customer = Single record.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Customer maintained externally is a reusable data object — Data reference is correct. Single record because each order has one customer. Embedded Data would copy the customer into each Case, creating stale data.

optionExplanations.A: The order references one independently maintained Customer record.
optionExplanations.B: Embedding fresh customer details would duplicate the shared source in each order.
optionExplanations.C: A Query can display sourced data, but the design asks for a keyed Customer association.
optionExplanations.D: The scenario describes a CRM data record rather than a Pega Customer Case.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A 'Billing Dispute' Case must reference the original 'Service Request' Case to access its data. The user selects the relevant Case from a list. Which Field Type models this?

options.text: Case reference — used when one Case must reference and reuse data from another Pega Case
Embedded Data — the Service Request data is entered freshly into the Billing Dispute by the user
Data reference — the Service Request is treated as an external data object maintained outside Pega
Query — fetches the Service Request details read-only using the Case ID as a parameter

practiceQuiz.hint: Reusing data FROM another Pega Case = Case reference.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Case reference models an association to another Pega Case, here the original Service Request. It expresses the relationship without requiring duplicated fields.

optionExplanations.A: Case reference expresses the relationship to the existing Service Request Case.
optionExplanations.B: Manual entry would duplicate details rather than reference the source Case.
optionExplanations.C: The source here is another Pega Case, not an ordinary external data object.
optionExplanations.D: A lookup may show details, but Case reference explicitly models the Case association.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A 'Medical Appointment' Case must show a physician's available time slots filtered by physician ID and a 2-week date range. The slots are read-only. Which Field Type supports this?

options.text: Query — provides read-only, parameter-driven access to external data (physician ID + date range as parameters)
Embedded Data — the available slots are entered manually by the user into the Case
Case reference — the appointment slots are sourced from a separate Pega 'Schedule' Case
Data reference — associate the selected physician record instead of querying time slots

practiceQuiz.hint: Read-only + parameter-driven filter of external data = Query Field Type.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Query fits the read-only availability lookup filtered by physician and date range. Data reference instead models a keyed association to reusable records and is not universally restricted to one record.

optionExplanations.A: Query fits the read-only lookup filtered by physician and date range.
optionExplanations.B: Manual embedded slot entry contradicts the sourced availability requirement.
optionExplanations.C: The scenario does not describe appointment slots as separate Pega Cases.
optionExplanations.D: A selected physician reference does not itself describe the filtered time-slot lookup.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA must choose a Field Type for a data relationship. The design brief says: 'The data is sourced from OUTSIDE the Case; we need to READ it but never write back to it; and we need to pass parameters to filter the results.' Which type matches ALL three constraints?

options.text: Query — provides read-only access to external data and supports passing parameters to filter/retrieve a specific subset of records
Data reference — associate a selected reusable record rather than model the filtered results
Embedded Data — captures user-entered data directly in the Case; parameters can be set as default values on the embedded fields
Case reference — references another Case's data; supports parameters to select which Case fields to expose as read-only

practiceQuiz.hint: Three constraints: external source + read-only + parameter-driven filtering. Which type matches all three?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Query fits the parameterized read-only lookup. Data reference models a keyed reusable-record association; it is not inherently a promise of write-back, and its underlying Data Pages can also use parameters.

optionExplanations.A: Query directly models the parameterized read-only lookup requested.
optionExplanations.B: A reusable keyed object association is different from this read-only query requirement.
optionExplanations.C: Embedded values originate in the Case rather than the required sourced lookup.
optionExplanations.D: Case reference associates another Case rather than this general filtered data source.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An order Case lets a customer add multiple products to a cart. For each product the user enters a quantity directly in the Case. Which Field Type and cardinality model the product list?

options.text: Embedded Data, List of records — user-entered, Case-specific data with multiple items per order
Data reference, Single record — each product is sourced from an external catalog and only one can be selected
Query, List of records — the product list is fetched read-only from an external catalog with no user entry
Case reference, Single record — each product line item references a separate Pega Product Case

practiceQuiz.hint: User enters quantities directly in the Case for many items → Embedded Data, List.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Each product line item is entered directly by the user (Embedded Data) and there can be many items per order (List of records). Single record would allow only one product; Data reference would point to an external object, not user-entered cart items.

optionExplanations.A: A list of embedded line items captures the quantities entered for this order.
optionExplanations.B: A single referenced Product cannot represent the order-specific list of quantities.
optionExplanations.C: A read-only query does not capture the editable quantities in each cart item.
optionExplanations.D: These line items are not independently processed Product Cases.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Within a 'Product line' Embedded Data object, each line item must reference one specific Product from an external catalog. Which Field Type and cardinality?

options.text: Data reference, Single record — the Product is sourced from an external catalog (reused) and one applies per line item
Embedded Data, Single record — each Product's details are entered fresh by the user for that line item
Query, List of records — the Product is fetched read-only from the catalog; multiple products apply per line
Case reference, Single record — each Product line item references a separate Product Case in Pega

practiceQuiz.hint: Externally sourced and reused = Data reference; one product per line = Single record.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Each Product line refers to one independently maintained catalog Product, so Data reference with Single record fits. The containing order can hold a list of these line items.

optionExplanations.A: One shared Product is referenced from each embedded Product line item.
optionExplanations.B: Re-entering Product details would duplicate the independently maintained catalog record.
optionExplanations.C: A list of products conflicts with the one-Product-per-line requirement.
optionExplanations.D: The catalog entry is a data record, not a Product Case.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA reviews the delivery address captured as Embedded Data in an order. What does embedding imply about ownership and persistence?

options.text: The address belongs to that Case instance rather than an independently shared address record; embedding alone does not enforce access control
The address is automatically moved into an external shared system of record
Embedding automatically creates a separate Address Case Type
Embedded Data is not persisted anywhere — it exists only in session memory and is lost when the Case is closed

practiceQuiz.hint: Case-owned data is a modeling choice, not an authorization mechanism.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Embedded Data belongs to the containing Case and persists with it rather than becoming an independently shared record. Other processes may access Case data when authorized; embedding is not a security boundary.

optionExplanations.A: The address is Case-owned and persistent; authorization still controls access to Case data.
optionExplanations.B: Embedded values are not automatically moved into a shared external record.
optionExplanations.C: The relationship does not create a separate Address Case Type.
optionExplanations.D: Embedded Case data is persisted with the Case rather than only in session memory.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA asks an SA to clarify the difference between Query and Data reference Field Types. Which TWO statements correctly distinguish them?

options.text: Query provides read-only access to data external to the Case
Query supports parameters to return specific, filtered data from the external source
Query stores data inside the Case like Embedded Data but in a separate read-only field
Data reference is always read-only and parameter-driven, making it interchangeable with Query

practiceQuiz.hint: Query = read-only + parameter-driven external access. Data reference = reuse a whole external object.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Query suits reading sourced results filtered by parameters. Data reference associates keyed reusable records. Select based on usage and ownership rather than assuming all Data Pages are unparameterized.

optionExplanations.A: Query is suited to reading information sourced outside the current Case.
optionExplanations.B: Parameters can restrict the data returned by the sourced lookup.
optionExplanations.C: Query is not defined as an embedded, Case-owned data structure.
optionExplanations.D: Data reference is a keyed reusable-record association, not an interchangeable Query definition.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA explains why 'Customer' is defined as a data object instead of scattering individual fields across Case Types. What benefit does grouping fields in a data object provide?

options.text: A data object groups related fields that model a single real-world entity, providing a common, reusable context across all Case Types that need Customer data
A data object stores the application's Rulesets so related rules are kept together with the data they apply to
A data object authenticates users by grouping the fields needed for identity verification in one place
A data object caches its grouped fields in memory during Case processing to improve performance

practiceQuiz.hint: Grouping related fields under one entity = common context = reusability.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Customer data object supplies a reusable entity definition and common context for related fields. This avoids redefining the group for every Case Type; individual fields can also be reused.

optionExplanations.A: Grouping Customer fields establishes a reusable entity definition and common context.
optionExplanations.B: Rulesets package rules rather than becoming fields in the Customer entity.
optionExplanations.C: Authentication is separate from structuring Customer data.
optionExplanations.D: Caching belongs to sourcing/cache configuration rather than this grouping benefit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Customer object has a Billing Address embedded inside it. The Billing Address in turn references a Country (sourced from a lookup table). An SA asks: 'Can a data relationship exist inside another data object?' What is the answer and what does this pattern demonstrate?

options.text: Yes — a data relationship can exist inside another data object (e.g., Country as a Data reference inside the Address data object, which is embedded in Customer); this demonstrates nested data modeling
No — data relationships can only connect top-level data objects to Case Types; relationships inside other objects create circular references that Pega rejects
Yes, but only for Embedded Data — you can nest Embedded Data inside another data object, but Query, Data reference, and Case reference cannot be nested
No — data objects can only contain flat properties; if you need nested structure, you must use a separate Case Type with a child Case relationship

practiceQuiz.hint: Can a data object that is itself referenced by another object also contain relationships?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Nested data modeling is fully supported — Customer embeds Address, and Address has a Data reference to Country. This creates a clean, layered data structure with no flat-list limitations.

optionExplanations.A: A referenced Country can be nested in an Address embedded within Customer.
optionExplanations.B: Nesting does not inherently create an invalid circular reference.
optionExplanations.C: Nested relationships are not restricted to Embedded Data alone.
optionExplanations.D: Data objects can contain relationships rather than only primitive fields.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is designing data relationships. A BA asks: 'What are the four Field Types available for creating data relationships?' What is the correct answer?

options.text: Embedded Data, Data reference, Case reference, and Query
Text, Integer, Decimal, and Boolean — the four primitive field types
Single, List, Read-only, and Read-write — the four cardinality/access modes
Work, Data, Integration, and Query — the four class types in Pega's hierarchy

practiceQuiz.hint: For user-entered, external objects, other Cases, and read-only filtered external data.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The four relationship Field Types are Embedded Data, Data reference, Case reference and Query. Primitive types describe individual values; cardinality and class groups are separate concepts.

optionExplanations.A: These four types cover Case-owned input, shared records, other Cases and query results.
optionExplanations.B: Primitive types describe individual values rather than data associations.
optionExplanations.C: Cardinality and edit modes are dimensions of a design, not these four relationship types.
optionExplanations.D: Class groups are different from the data relationship Field Types.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A 'Patient Registration' Case requires collecting an emergency contact name and phone entered by the registering nurse at the point of care. The contact belongs specifically to this registration. Which Field Type is correct?

options.text: Embedded Data — user-entered, Case-specific data that lives with this registration Case instance
Data reference — the emergency contact is sourced from an external contact registry and reused across patient Cases
Case reference — the emergency contact is a separate Pega Case referenced from the registration
Query — the emergency contact data is fetched read-only from an HR system using the patient's ID as a parameter

practiceQuiz.hint: User enters it at registration + belongs only to this Case = Embedded Data.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Emergency contact details entered directly into the registration Case are user-entered and Case-specific — Embedded Data. External contacts maintained in a separate system would use Data reference instead.

optionExplanations.A: The registration-specific emergency contact is captured as embedded data.
optionExplanations.B: A reused external contact record is not the scenario described.
optionExplanations.C: The contact is a data group rather than an independently processed Case.
optionExplanations.D: An HR lookup would not capture the nurse-entered registration contact.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A 'Booking' Case must identify which medical facility the appointment is at. Facility records are maintained in a Facilities data object sourced from an external hospital management system. Which Field Type connects the Booking to the Facility?

options.text: Data reference — the Facility is a reusable data object maintained externally and referenced by the Booking Case
Embedded Data — facility details are entered by the user for each booking
Case reference — the Facility is a separate Pega Case referenced by the Booking Case
Query — facility data is fetched read-only from the hospital system with parameterized filters

practiceQuiz.hint: External data object reused in the Case = Data reference.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Facility maintained externally is a reusable data object — Data reference is correct for an externally-maintained object. Embedded Data would copy facility details into each Case, creating stale data if the facility changes.

optionExplanations.A: The Booking associates a shared Facility record maintained by the source system.
optionExplanations.B: Entering facility details anew would duplicate the maintained record.
optionExplanations.C: The Facility is described as a data object, not a Pega Case.
optionExplanations.D: A filtered read-only lookup differs from the requested Facility record association.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is modeling a 'Product line' data object that contains a reference to a 'Product' from an external catalog. A colleague asks: 'Can a data relationship reference one data object inside another?' What is the answer?

options.text: Yes — data relationships can reference one data object inside another, enabling nested data models such as Product inside Product line
No — data relationships can only connect data objects directly to Case Types, not to other data objects
Only for Query fields — Query is the only relationship type that supports nesting inside another data object
Only in Dev Studio — nested data object relationships cannot be configured in App Studio and require direct Ruleset editing

practiceQuiz.hint: Data relationships can be nested — a data object inside another data object is standard modeling.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Data relationships can reference one data object inside another — a Product line Embedded Data object can contain a Product Data reference. Relationships are not limited to top-level Case fields.

optionExplanations.A: The Product line object can contain its own reference to the shared Product.
optionExplanations.B: Relationships are not confined to direct Case Type associations.
optionExplanations.C: Nesting is not an exclusive feature of Query fields.
optionExplanations.D: Nested modeling is not defined as requiring manual Ruleset editing.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega developer is reviewing the four Data Relationship types available when designing a data model. Which TWO are valid Data Relationship types in Pega?

options.text: Embedded Data — related data is stored directly inside the parent Case without a separate reusable record
Case reference — the Case stores a reference to one or more other Cases by their Case ID
Linked record — a mirrored copy of the data is created in a separate database table automatically
Dynamic reference — a Decision Table determines which related record to load at runtime

practiceQuiz.hint: Recall the four Pega relationship types: Embedded Data, Data reference, Case reference, and Query.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Embedded Data stores related field data directly inside the parent Case — the data has no independent existence. Case reference stores the ID of one or more related Cases, linking them without copying their data. Linked record and Dynamic reference are not standard Pega Data Relationship types.

optionExplanations.A: Embedded Data captures related values owned by the containing Case.
optionExplanations.B: Case reference models an association to another Case rather than copying its fields.
optionExplanations.C: Linked record is not one of the four standard relationship Field Types here.
optionExplanations.D: A Decision Table can supply logic but does not create a Dynamic reference Field Type.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is designing a customer record where address details (street, city, postal code) are nested within the customer Case and do not exist as standalone reusable records. Which TWO statements correctly describe this scenario?

options.text: Embedded Data is the correct relationship type — the address fields are stored inside the parent Case
The address Data Object is embedded with a cardinality of Single, since each customer has one primary address
A Data reference should be used because the address data is displayed within the same Case form
A Query relationship is required because address data must be retrieved from an external system at runtime

practiceQuiz.hint: When data exists only inside the parent and is not reused elsewhere, Embedded Data with a cardinality is the pattern.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Embedded Data fits the Case-owned address; Single record matches one primary address. Query is for read-only results sourced outside the Case, which need not mean outside Pega.

optionExplanations.A: The address values belong to the parent Case rather than a shared source record.
optionExplanations.B: Single record matches the one primary address specified.
optionExplanations.C: Displaying a field on the same form does not decide its data ownership.
optionExplanations.D: There is no external retrieval requirement for this Case-owned address.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega application models a Customer Case where each customer can have multiple Insurance Policies, and each Policy exists as an independent reusable data record associated with exactly one Customer. Which TWO statements correctly describe how to model this relationship?

options.text: The relationship type is Data reference — the Policy records exist independently and are referenced from the Customer Case by ID
The cardinality is List of records — one Customer Case can reference multiple Policy records
The relationship type is Embedded Data — the Policy data is stored inside the Customer Case with no independent existence
The cardinality is Single — a Customer Case can only ever reference exactly one related Policy record

practiceQuiz.hint: Policies exist independently (Data reference) and one customer has many policies (Many cardinality).
practiceQuiz.rationale: Because Insurance Policies exist as independent reusable records — not as data embedded within the Customer Case — the correct relationship type is Data reference. The cardinality is Many because a single Customer can be associated with multiple Policies. Embedded Data would be wrong here because Policies have independent existence and identity.

optionExplanations.A: Independent Policy records are reused through a Data reference relationship.
optionExplanations.B: List of records matches the multiple policies associated with one Customer.
optionExplanations.C: Embedding would give policies Case-specific ownership rather than independent identity.
optionExplanations.D: Single record contradicts the stated multiple-policy requirement.

quickRecap.value: Groups related fields to model an entity (common context); reusable across Case Types; can reference other objects.
Container that relates data but stores none; relates object↔Case Type, object↔object, Case Type↔Case Type.
Embedded Data: Case-owned input; Data reference: maintained local or external records; Case reference: another Case; Query: read-only results outside the Case, with parameters.
Single record (one set) vs. List of records (many sets) — chosen independently of the Field Type.
In-case input → Embedded; external object reuse → Data reference; another Case → Case reference; parameterized read-only lookup → Query.
